stimulus:
The Osborne Fire Finder is a strange little instrument: a round map table with a brass ring and two sighting hairs, bolted to the middle of a cabin. You swing the alidade until smoke sits in the notch, read the azimuth, and call it in. Two towers calling in bearings give you a crossing point, and the fire has to be where the lines cross. That is triangulation, the same trick as surveying and old ship navigation, done with a pencil and a telephone.

The telephone is its own oddity. Early lines were often strung along tree trunks, or even single wire with ground return, so lightning was a hazard to the person holding the handset. That's why some towers had glass insulator stools. Lookouts stood on them during storms, which is a funny image: a person on a glass-footed stool in a glass-walled room, watching the sky that might hit them.

Glass walls make me think of cupolas and widow's walks, rooms built purely for looking. Then Jack Kerouac, who spent a summer on Desolation Peak in 1956 and wrote about boredom and clouds. Edward Abbey did it too. Boredom turns out to be a job requirement, apparently, like attentiveness's awkward cousin.

Now cameras and algorithms scan ridgelines for smoke. They never get lonely, and they never leave notes in the logbook about mice.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Two-bearing triangulation of AP-1 occupancy and chromatin state
ideas.description: Like two towers' bearings crossing at a fire, intersect two independent readouts at the same loci after a transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or injury): AP-1 (FOS/JUN) ChIP/CUT&RUN occupancy and ATAC-seq accessibility or H3K27ac. Loci where both persist long after the stimulus ends, and AP-1 motif-containing sites are the only overlap, are candidate memory sites.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after the stimulus has ended (necessity test for maintenance)
ideas.description: Prime cells, wash out the stimulus, and after a rest period add a dTAG/AID degron or dominant-negative (A-FOS) to remove AP-1 only during the memory phase. Compare accessibility and the faster secondary response on restimulation to controls; loss of memory when AP-1 is removed after induction shows AP-1 is required to maintain it, not only to establish it.

ideas.title: Sufficiency by optogenetic or chemogenetic AP-1 pulses
ideas.description: Drive FOS/JUN activity with a light- or drug-inducible system in naive cells using pulses of different duration and frequency, then measure persistent chromatin opening and altered transcriptional responses to a later unrelated stimulus. This tests whether AP-1 activity alone can write a lasting state and how its dynamics encode dose or history.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-tracked memory persistence and heritability
ideas.description: Use live reporters of AP-1 activity (e.g., FOS-GFP) with time-lapse imaging or barcoded lineages plus scRNA/scATAC to track whether primed state passes through cell divisions and how many generations it lasts. Like the lookout's logbook, this gives a time-stamped record per cell, showing whether the state is bistable or heritable versus a decaying signal.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like activity and cofactor dependence at primed enhancers
ideas.description: Mutate or CRISPR-delete AP-1 motifs at specific primed enhancers, and use CUT&Tag, BAF/SWI-SNF inhibition, and Micro-C to test whether AP-1 recruits remodelers and holds loops open. Reporter assays for memory (faster reinduction of the linked gene) will show whether site-specific AP-1 binding is causal, versus alternatives like other TFs or DNA methylation.
